source: Passenger help guide. Informational only — not compensation policy.

articles.title: Book a flight
articles.text: I can help you plan a new booking. I need origin, destination, travel date, and how many passengers. This prototype has no live inventory, so I will not invent a flight number or fare. Once those slots are filled I will confirm the request and hand a supervisor the details if you want it ticketed.

articles.title: Check-in
articles.text: Web check-in usually opens 48 hours before departure. Bring a photo ID that matches the name on the booking. If your current flight is delayed or cancelled, check-in for that leg is handled as a disruption, not a new booking.

articles.title: Baggage
articles.text: Cabin and checked-bag allowances depend on the fare you bought. I cannot waive excess-baggage fees. If a bag was delayed or damaged on this disruption, say so and I will open a supervisor case — that is not a meal-voucher or hotel entitlement.

articles.title: Seats
articles.text: Seat changes on an operating flight are a booking-assist request, not compensation. I will not invent a seat map. If the airline cancelled the flight, free rebooking within 24 hours is the disruption rule, not a free seat upgrade.

articles.title: New trip versus this disruption
articles.text: For this disrupted booking I can apply the airline's delay and cancellation rules only. For a new trip I can collect origin, destination, date, and passenger count. I cannot invent extra compensation, flight numbers, or fares.
